video_specification.overview:
Produce a {DURATION_SECONDS}-second {TONE} video about {TOPIC}. The final deliverable is a rendered MP4 at {WIDTH}x{HEIGHT} {FPS}fps generated by Remotion, with continuous narration synthesized via ElevenLabs and a caption overlay synced to the audio.
Visual style: {VISUAL_STYLE}. Every frame has a dynamic visual underneath the captions — there are no static text-on-background shots. Visual cuts vary in duration based on visual complexity, not on narration length.

prerequisites.environment_setup: - ELEVENLABS_API_KEY is exported in the shell environment - ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID optionally overrides the default voice (Rachel) - Node 20+ and pnpm are available - The Remotion project is pre-scaffolded by the harness with package.json, tsconfig.json, src/Root.tsx (placeholder), src/anchors.ts (stub), src/Captions.tsx (caption overlay, do not edit), src/shots/ (empty), public/, vitest.config.ts. - Do not touch package.json dependencies unless explicitly required.

technology_stack.audio_format: MP3 from ElevenLabs, served from public/audio.mp3

pacing_rules.rule: Every frame must have a dynamic visual. Static frames are forbidden.
Captions are an overlay. No shot exists just to display text.

Shot duration is set by VISUAL COMPLEXITY, not by narration length: - complex: 4–8 seconds (data viz, multi-element animation, charts) - simple: 1–2.5 seconds (single icon/image with motion drift) - transition: 0.3–0.8 seconds (wipes, fades, slides)
Complex shots should be roughly 3–4x longer than simple shots. Contrast creates rhythm.
Anchors are emphasis sync points. Declare an anchor only when a specific shot needs to land an animation on a specific narration word. Aim for 1 anchor per ~10 seconds. Skipping is fine.

video_specification.narrative_arc:
{NARRATIVE_ARC_PROSE}
Three to five sentences describing what the audience learns and in what order. This is the input to Phase A which writes the continuous narration. Do NOT write the literal voiceover here.

anchor.purpose: {What visual event lands on which narration word}

step.title: Phase A — Director
step.tasks: - Read video_spec.xml - Write script.json with continuous narration, shots[], anchors[] - Stop

step.title: Phase B — Shot components (parallel, capped at 5 concurrent)
step.tasks: - One shot agent per timing.shots[i] - Each writes src/shots/Shot{NN}.tsx + Shot{NN}.anchors.json - Continuous motion, no static frames, no caption rendering

step.title: Phase C — Compositor
step.tasks: - Assemble src/Root.tsx with Audio, shot Sequences, Captions overlay - Run vitest alignment test - Run `npx remotion render` → out/video.mp4

success_criteria.functionality: - alignment.test.ts passes (every declared anchor within ±1 frame) - out/video.mp4 exists and plays end-to-end - Captions overlay renders synchronized text on every spoken frame - No shot is just text on a background - Complex shots are visibly longer than simple shots
